turns.speaker: practitioner
turns.text: Thanks for coming in. What would you like us to focus on today?

codes.evidence_quote: What would you like us to focus on today?
codes.rationale: Open question that lets the client choose the topic.

codes.evidence_quote: What would you like us to focus on
codes.rationale: Invites the client to set the agenda, sharing control of the session.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: My doctor keeps telling me I need to move more. I sit at a desk all day, and by the time I get home I'm wiped out.
turns.client_evidence_quote: by the time I get home I'm wiped out

turns.speaker: practitioner
turns.text: You're hearing it from your doctor, and at the same time your days leave you with not much left in the tank.

codes.evidence_quote: at the same time your days leave you with not much left in the tank
codes.rationale: Joins the doctor's advice with the client's exhaustion, adding meaning beyond the client's words.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Exactly. I know walking would help. I used to walk all the time before this job.

turns.speaker: practitioner
turns.text: Walking used to be a regular part of your life. What did you like about it back then?

codes.evidence_quote: Walking used to be a regular part of your life.
codes.rationale: Restates what the client said with little added meaning.

codes.evidence_quote: What did you like about it back then?
codes.rationale: Open question that draws out the client's own reasons.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: It cleared my head. I'd come back from a walk and actually feel like myself again.
turns.client_evidence_quote: I'd come back from a walk and actually feel like myself again.

turns.speaker: practitioner
turns.text: Walking was more than exercise for you. It was how you found your way back to yourself.

codes.evidence_quote: It was how you found your way back to yourself.
codes.rationale: Reflects the personal meaning walking had, beyond what the client said.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Yeah. I miss that, honestly.

turns.speaker: practitioner
turns.text: Part of you really wants that feeling back.

codes.evidence_quote: Part of you really wants that feeling back.
codes.rationale: Reflects an unstated desire for change.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I do. I just don't see where it fits. My mornings are chaos with the kids.
turns.client_evidence_quote: I just don't see where it fits.

turns.speaker: practitioner
turns.text: You keep a demanding job and a busy family running, which takes real persistence. Where in your week might a walk fit, if anywhere?

codes.rationale: Names a genuine strength of the client.

codes.evidence_quote: Where in your week might a walk fit, if anywhere?
codes.rationale: Open question that leaves room for the client to say no.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Maybe lunch. We get an hour, and I usually just eat at my desk.

turns.speaker: practitioner
turns.text: Lunch is a window that's already there.

codes.evidence_quote: Lunch is a window that's already there.
codes.rationale: Simple restatement of the client's idea.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: It is. Even twenty minutes would be something.
turns.client_evidence_quote: Even twenty minutes would be something.

turns.speaker: practitioner
turns.text: Twenty minutes feels doable, and it sounds like it would really matter to you.

codes.evidence_quote: Twenty minutes feels doable, and it sounds like it would really matter to you.
codes.rationale: Reflects both ability and importance, going beyond the client's words.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: It would. I guess I worry what my coworkers would think if I'm the only one leaving.
turns.client_evidence_quote: I worry what my coworkers would think

turns.speaker: practitioner
turns.text: Being the one who walks out feels a bit exposed, and it's completely your call. What might make it easier?

codes.evidence_quote: Being the one who walks out feels a bit exposed
codes.rationale: Reflects the feeling underneath the coworker concern.
Explicitly affirms that the choice belongs to the client.
Open question inviting the client's own solution.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: If I asked Dana to come with me, it wouldn't feel so strange. She's always complaining about sitting too.
turns.client_evidence_quote: If I asked Dana to come with me, it wouldn't feel so strange.

turns.speaker: practitioner
turns.text: A walking partner would turn it into something you do together instead of something you sneak off to do.

codes.evidence_quote: turn it into something you do together instead of something you sneak off to do
codes.rationale: Reframes the client's idea in a way that adds meaning.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: Right. I think I'll ask her tomorrow.
turns.client_evidence_quote: I think I'll ask her tomorrow.

turns.speaker: practitioner
turns.text: You've gone from not seeing where walking fits to a plan to ask Dana tomorrow.

codes.evidence_quote: You've gone from not seeing where walking fits to a plan to ask Dana tomorrow.
codes.rationale: Summary that links the client's starting point to their plan.

turns.speaker: client
turns.text: I'll text myself a reminder at noon so I don't talk myself out of it.
turns.client_evidence_quote: I'll text myself a reminder at noon

globals.rationale: Consistently drew out and reinforced the client's own reasons, desire and plan for walking (for example T9 and T21).
Met the time and coworker concerns with reflection and autonomy support instead of arguing, without dwelling on barriers.
